newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HES says expects H1 loss of NLG 22.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: HES says expects H1 loss of NLG 22.6 mln.

text.p: Transport and storage group Hes Beheer said on Thursday it expected to suffer a loss of 22.6 million guilders over the first half of this year.
It added it expected a modest 1997 full-year profit from ordinary operations, but due to extraordinary charges the total result would be negative.

HES said 1997 would be a transition year for the company, after which a rising trend in results was expected. Falling turnover would be offset by structurally lower cost levels, higher productivity and lower interest charges.
A previously announced refinancing of the company, which was approved by Hes's shareholders today, had given the company substantially more financial leeway.
"In the short and medium-term, the management board will mainly focus on a further strengthening of the company's financial position," Hes said.
Hes, which will publish its first-half figures on August 6, said the expected half-year net loss of 22.6 million guilders was caused by extraordinary charges of 23.8 million guilders.

This included a 17.6 million guilder provision for a loss-making investment in Brazil. Hes said it was taking measures to improve the results of this unit and was studying possibilities of joining forces with other partners there.

The extraordinary charges also included a 1.7 million guilder write-off on a debt owed by Ireland's bankrupt shipping operator Bell Lines and a 4.5 million guilder payment to ABN AMRO Bank for the redemption of a loan.
